A clear Pareto improvement in accuracy vs. cost would confirm the hypothesis; parity or degradation would refute it.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of attention complexity and routing overhead: derive the expected FLOPs and memory scaling of learned routing mechanisms (e.g., top-k gating with auxiliary load-balancing losses) relative to full dense attention, under varying sequence lengths and expert counts. — Provides a formal framework to predict whether sparse routing can achieve sub-quadratic scaling in sequence length without sacrificing representational capacity. If theory shows an irreducible overhead that cancels out efficiency gains at scale, the hypothesis is weakened.

If the majority of studies show that learned routing attention matches or outperforms dense attention at scale, confidence in the hypothesis increases; if not, it suggests the hypothesis is likely false.
